categories.rationale: The repository consistently reuses central API, Zotero, persistence and presentation abstractions; no semantic duplicate responsibility was established.
Browser, transport, integration and persistence boundaries are explicit; no repository-wide redesign is warranted.
Audit mode has no base/head attribution scope, so introduced-change proportionality cannot be scored.
Control flow and validation are generally explicit, but sync error handling violates its checkpoint completion contract.
Pages reuse the shared API client and PaperCard; responsibility was assessed by behavior rather than component length.
Most state is local or derived, but collection identity and result state can become incoherent under response reordering.
Listener cleanup and search stale-response protection are present, while two user-facing async paths have deterministically unsafe completion ownership.
The Svelte application has proportionate page, component, service and PDF utility boundaries without speculative wrappers.
Request context is concurrency-safe, but attachment buffering and synchronous ZIP inflation create an unbounded event-loop resource path.
Queries are user scoped and schema constraints/indexes correspond to concrete access paths; no plan-backed performance defect was asserted.
Zotero version preconditions protect note and delete writes, but the incremental cache checkpoint is not consistent with partial failures.
One fetch path has a deadline, but arbitrary destination access and missing Zotero deadlines materially weaken the network boundary.
The architecture favors asynchronous I/O, but large attachment handling is unbounded; impact remains suspected without measurements.
Metadata caching is part of the product, but no remote-cache requirement or cache stampede path was evidenced; Redis absence is neutral.
Contextual error logs exist, but no metrics, traces, query counts, latency distributions, load tests or reproducible performance measurements were found.
